Name: Hide foreign key columns
Description: Foreign key columns in fact tables should be hidden from report view. They should be used for relationships only.
Expression: !IsHidden && Table.ObjectType == "Table" && Name.EndsWith("Key") && Table.UsedInRelationships.Any(FromTable == Table && FromColumn == outerIt)
Remarks: Keys used in relationships must not be visible to report consumers.

Name: Avoid bidirectional relationships
Description: Bidirectional cross-filter causes ambiguous filter paths and unpredictable measure results. Use CROSSFILTER() in DAX instead.
Remarks: This model deliberately uses single-direction filters only.

Name: Add descriptions to complex measures
Description: Measures with more than 2 DAX lines or using CALCULATE should have a description for self-service users.
Remarks: Descriptions show up in the field list tooltip.

Name: Use DIVIDE() instead of /
Description: Direct division with / will return an error on divide-by-zero. Use DIVIDE(numerator, denominator) for safe division.

Name: Numeric measures must have a format string
Description: Numeric measures without a format string will display raw decimal values to report users.

Name: Avoid filtering columns with implicit =
Description: CALCULATE( expr, Table[Column] = "Value" ) is a shorthand that bypasses context transition. Use KEEPFILTERS or explicit FILTER when needed.

Name: Remove unused columns
Description: Columns not used in relationships, measures, calculated columns, or visuals inflate the model size.

Name: Text columns used in sorting must have SortByColumn set
Description: Month names, levels, bands etc. must be sorted by an integer column, not alphabetically.
Expression: DataType == DataType.String && string.IsNullOrEmpty(SortByColumn?.Name) && (Name.Contains("Month") || Name.Contains("Band") || Name.Contains("Level") || Name.Contains("Stage"))

Name: Calendar table must be marked as a date table
Description: Without marking the Calendar as a date table, DAX time-intelligence functions may return incorrect results.

Name: Prefer RELATED() over LOOKUPVALUE() in calculated columns
Description: RELATED() uses the existing relationship path and is faster than LOOKUPVALUE() for related table lookups.
